pathogens-s1.title: Six infectious diseases and how they spread
pathogens-s1.html:
Pathogen type and main route of spread (summarized from WHO fact sheets)
DiseasePathogenMain route of spread
Malariaprotozoan (Plasmodium)bites of Anopheles mosquitoes
Cholerabacteriumwater or food contaminated with feces

pathogens-s2.title: A mosquito-borne disease cycle and a warming climate

options: A bacterium, virus or other agent that causes disease
An animal, such as a mosquito, that carries disease to people
A chemical pollutant that builds up in body fat
An illness that does not pass from person to person

items.q: In the spread of malaria, what is the role of the Anopheles mosquito?
options: It is the pathogen that infects people’s red blood cells
It is the vector: it carries the parasite between people
It is the host that becomes sick with malaria symptoms
It kills the parasite before it can reach people

items.q: Which disease in the table spreads mainly through water or food contaminated with feces?
options: Malaria
Tuberculosis
Cholera
Zika virus

items.q: Which two diseases in the table are spread by the same kind of vector?
options: Cholera and tuberculosis, both spread by mosquitoes
Plague and cholera, both spread by fleas
Tuberculosis and plague, both spread by drinking water
Malaria and West Nile virus, both spread by mosquitoes

items.q: For which disease in the table would building sewage treatment plants and safe water supplies do the most to cut cases?
options: Cholera
Plague
West Nile virus
Tuberculosis

items.q: A region reported 2,400 cholera cases in the year before its main city opened a water treatment plant, and 600 cases the year after. What was the percent change in cases?

mistakes.why: You divided by the new value. Percent change is (new − old) ÷ old × 100: (600 − 2,400) ÷ 2,400 × 100.
The size is right but cases fell, so the change is negative: (600 − 2,400) ÷ 2,400 × 100 = −75%.

items.q: In the diagram, which step moves the pathogen from an infected person to a mosquito?
options: Step 2: the mosquito flies to another person
Step 3: the healthy person becomes sick
Step 1: the mosquito bites the infected person
The infected person drinks water the mosquito laid eggs in

items.q: According to the diagram, why might a warming climate increase the number of people at risk from a mosquito-borne disease?
options: Warmer air kills the pathogen inside the mosquito
Warmer weather makes people’s blood easier for pathogens to grow in
Hotter summers make mosquitoes stop biting people
Milder winters let the mosquito survive farther from the equator

items.q: Which action would break the cycle in the diagram at the vector?
options: Draining standing water where mosquitoes lay their eggs
Treating the town’s drinking water with chlorine
Asking sick people to cover their mouths when they cough
Cooking meat to a higher temperature

items.q: Explain how warmer temperatures could increase cases of a mosquito-borne disease.

specific.frame: If temperatures ___, then the mosquito’s range will ___, because ___.

change.label: Change
options: rise
fall
stay the same

why.1: The question is about warmer temperatures, a rise.
why.2: With no change in temperature, the range would not shift.

direction.label: Range
options: expand toward the poles and to higher elevations
shrink toward the equator
stay where it is

why.1: Warming opens cooler places to mosquitoes; the range grows, not shrinks.
why.2: Warming changes where mosquitoes can survive.

because.label: Because
options: milder winters let more mosquitoes survive in places that were too cold
warm air kills the pathogen
mosquitoes move to follow cooler water

why.1: If warming killed the pathogen, cases would fall.
why.2: Mosquitoes need warmth to breed; they spread into newly warm areas.

specific.model: If temperatures rise, then the mosquito’s range will expand toward the poles, because milder winters let more mosquitoes survive in places that were too cold, so more people are bitten and cases increase.

items.q: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease that spreads through the air when an infected person coughs. Why does it spread most in crowded, poorly ventilated housing?
options: Crowded housing has more mosquitoes, which carry tuberculosis
Tuberculosis bacteria grow in standing water near buildings
Close, shared air spreads bacteria from coughs
Crowding makes people’s blood a better home for bacteria

items.q: Plague is caused by a bacterium that lives in rodents. How does it most often reach people?
options: Through drinking water contaminated with sewage
Through the bites of mosquitoes that fed on infected birds
Through eating vegetables grown in polluted soil
Through the bites of fleas that fed on infected rodents

items.q: Which statement about SARS and MERS is correct?
options: Both are respiratory viruses that came from animals
Both are bacterial diseases spread by drinking dirty water
Both are spread mainly through the bites of mosquitoes
Both are caused by protozoa living in red blood cells

items.q: Which conditions help infectious diseases spread in developing countries? Select all that apply.
options: Lack of sewage treatment, so feces reach drinking water
Limited access to health care and medicines
Winters cold enough to kill most mosquitoes
A high share of homes with piped, treated water

items.q: How can a pathogen evolve resistance to the drugs used to treat it?
options: Each pathogen learns to avoid the drug during its own lifetime
The drug changes the pathogen’s DNA so that it becomes resistant
Drugs kill sensitive individuals, so resistant ones survive and reproduce
People’s bodies make the drug weaker the more they take it

items.q: Which change linked to climate change could increase waterborne disease after heavy storms?
options: Less ultraviolet light reaching the surface of the water
Colder water that slows the growth of bacteria
Lower sea levels that drain coastal wetlands
Floods that push sewage into drinking water
